components.title: Midwest diesel rises 6.9% in a second consecutive weekly jump
components.summary: EIA’s 21 September Midwest diesel benchmark is $6.680/gal, up $0.430 from $6.250 (+6.9%) after the prior week’s 5.1% rise. The prior public escalation trigger was crossed; Watershed’s actual carrier surcharge, lane mix and pass-through remain unknown.
components.factorRationale: Exposure 75: public facility geography makes truck freight plausible, but mode and miles are unmeasured. Severity 80: the benchmark reached $6.680/gal and rose 6.9% in one week. Confidence 70: primary EIA measurement, with no company contract or invoice. Persistence 80: two consecutive weekly increases above 5%, supported by the separate EIA distillate-constraint scenario. Velocity 80: weekly repricing can reach surcharges quickly. Dependency 80 and substitutability 35: road freight is operationally important and near-term fuel substitution is limited, but actual carrier terms are unknown.
components.causalPath: Regional retail diesel benchmark ↑ → applicable carrier fuel surcharge or freight quote ↑ → delivered input/outbound cost and conditional margin or service pressure.
components.verify: Current carrier surcharge tables and invoices, contract lag, lane and mode mix, outbound miles, customer pass-through and any tender or service refusal.
components.action: CFO and Supply Chain should reconcile current carrier surcharge tables and invoices, estimate next-cycle margin and OTIF exposure, and confirm customer pass-through before new commitments.
components.trigger: A third consecutive >5% weekly rise, actual contracted transport cost >5% above plan, a tender/service refusal, or a verified customer-service impact.
components.dateNote: EIA released the data on 22 September 2026; the price reference week is 21 September. This is a regional retail benchmark, not a Watershed freight rate or realized loss.
components.coverageChange: Crossed the prior public trigger: a second consecutive weekly rise above 5%. Guidance changes to immediate invoice/contract verification; no realized company loss or urgent continuity event is asserted.

components.title: Grain outlook tightens; specialty basis still unknown
components.summary: September WASDE projects U.S. total-grain ending stocks of 62.92 Mt versus 65.03 Mt in August. That is a broad context signal, not a popcorn forecast.
components.factorRationale: Broad grain balance → potential feed/grain pricing → formula costs. All seven factors are uncalibrated proxies (45/55/45/80/45/55/60); popping-grade corn and food-grade contracts can diverge materially.
components.causalPath: Broad grain balance → potential feed/grain pricing → formula costs. All seven factors are uncalibrated proxies (45/55/45/80/45/55/60); popping-grade corn and food-grade contracts can diverge materially.
components.verify: Actual grains, specification basis, origin, contracts and inventory cover.
components.action: Track supplier quotations before changing coverage or formulations.
components.trigger: Two relevant supplier quotes worsen >10%, or verified cover falls below the approved operating threshold.

components.title: Traceability planning requires a product-form decision
components.summary: FDA describes a proposed extension and a congressional direction not to enforce the rule before 20 July 2028. Applicability still depends on covered food and form.
components.factorRationale: Covered receiving/transformation → KDE/CTE obligations → systems and partner coordination. Scope is not established for Watershed; factors 55/65/65/90/25/70/60 reflect planning exposure rather than a violation.
components.causalPath: Covered receiving/transformation → KDE/CTE obligations → systems and partner coordination. Scope is not established for Watershed; factors 55/65/65/90/25/70/60 reflect planning exposure rather than a violation.
components.verify: Food Traceability List applicability at each process stage; exemptions; customer contractual dates.
components.action: Quality and IT should map covered inputs and data exchanges, retaining product-specific legal review.
components.trigger: Final regulatory change, customer deadline, or a confirmed gap in an applicable traceability process.

components.title: Pet formats offer a qualified commercial opening
components.summary: APPA projects $69.7bn of pet-food and treat sales for 2026. This does not establish unit growth or freeze-dried segment growth.
components.factorRationale: Pet-category spending → candidate launch budgets → topper/inclusion projects suited to advertised capabilities. Factors 70/60/45/85/45/65/65 reflect an unvalidated sales hypothesis, not Watershed revenue.
components.causalPath: Pet-category spending → candidate launch budgets → topper/inclusion projects suited to advertised capabilities. Factors 70/60/45/85/45/65/65 reflect an unvalidated sales hypothesis, not Watershed revenue.
components.verify: Premium segment units, brand launch plans, current capacity and qualified process fit.
components.action: Build a small list of qualified topper/inclusion prospects and test demand before reserving capacity.
components.trigger: Documented customer briefs and trial conversion, with confirmed available capacity and validated safety controls.
components.dateNote: APPA projection publication date unverified; baseline evidence, not a new event on retrieval day.

components.title: Popcorn expansion is an opportunity to verify
components.summary: Deer Creek’s public directory now lists Aunt Em’s / Heartland together. The reported equipment transition remains unverified as completed.
components.factorRationale: Announced process additions → possible new formats → private-label prospects. Factors 70/65/60/85/40/75/60 assume qualification work; no incremental capacity is counted as operational.
components.causalPath: Announced process additions → possible new formats → private-label prospects. Factors 70/65/60/85/40/75/60 assume qualification work; no incremental capacity is counted as operational.
components.verify: Equipment ownership, commissioning, production qualification and available slots.
components.action: Confirm the production milestone before offering new formats or delivery commitments.
components.trigger: Verified commissioned capacity plus a qualified customer opportunity.

components.title: Baby-food lead guidance has a material scope exclusion
components.summary: The FDA final guidance excludes grain-based and freeze-dried snacks. It must not be applied automatically to every toddler product.
components.factorRationale: SKU classification → applicable contaminant requirements/customer specifications → testing and release criteria. Low velocity 20 reflects an existing rule, not new contamination. Other factors are analytical prioritization.
components.causalPath: SKU classification → applicable contaminant requirements/customer specifications → testing and release criteria. Low velocity 20 reflects an existing rule, not new contamination. Other factors are analytical prioritization.
components.verify: Each SKU’s form, age positioning, state rules and customer specifications.
components.action: Keep contaminant controls; have Quality document the correct guidance scope by SKU.
components.trigger: Changed FDA/state requirements or an actual out-of-spec result; then use the approved food-safety response process.

components.title: Ingredient benchmarks diverge: grains up, dairy down
components.summary: August BLS PPI: grains +4.3% and oilseeds +3.9% month over month (SA); dairy products -1.0% (NSA). These broad benchmarks cannot be netted into a Watershed cost change without actual purchasing weights.
components.factorRationale: Exposure 60: advertised platforms imply plausible input channels, not measured spend. Severity 50: material benchmark moves with offsets. Confidence 60: primary data but unknown purchase basis. Persistence 65: possible contract lag; velocity 50: one monthly observation. Dependency 65: ingredient relevance; substitutability 65: broad alternatives subject to quality/customer approval. All factors are provisional judgments.
components.causalPath: Grain/oilseed and dairy benchmark divergence → category-specific vendor quotes and contract resets → conditional product margins.
components.verify: Actual ingredient basket, food-grade specifications, quote dates, contract basis, inventory cover and customer pass-through.
components.action: Compare the next quotes for grain, seed and dairy categories separately; quantify net effect only after purchasing weights are supplied.
components.trigger: A relevant delivered quote rises >5% against plan or confirmed pass-through fails to offset a sustained input increase.
components.dateNote: Reference August 2026; July-to-August changes. Preliminary. Oilseeds are not a pumpkin-seed quote; grains are not a food-grade popcorn quote.
components.coverageChange: Newly assessed coverage; not evidence that the event began on retrieval day.

components.title: Metro labor context remains mixed
components.summary: July preliminary NSA unemployment: Bloomington 3.3% (June 4.0%), Peoria 3.8% (4.5%), Milwaukee-Waukesha 3.8% (3.8%). Bloomington and Peoria manufacturing employment was 1.2% and 0.9% below a year earlier. This does not establish a Watershed shortage.
components.factorRationale: Exposure 65: relevant regional operating presence. Severity 45: labor-market context without company vacancies. Confidence 45 in the conditional channel, reduced by metro aggregation and seasonality. Persistence 65 and velocity 30: lagged monthly data. Dependency 65: manufacturing staffing. Substitutability 65: unmeasured local alternatives. These are judgments, not a shortage estimate.
components.causalPath: Regional hiring conditions → conditional recruitment and retention difficulty → staffing, throughput and overtime.
components.verify: Time to fill by trade and site, accepted wage rates, overtime, turnover, vacancy counts and actual recruiting catchments.
components.action: Use metro data to frame a hiring review; compare it with actual recruiting results before changing staffing or pay assumptions.
components.trigger: Critical maintenance/production roles remain unfilled >45 days or persistent overtime exceeds the approved site plan.
components.dateNote: Reference July 2026, preliminary and not seasonally adjusted. Exact release day unverified; retrieved September 17. Monthly declines can be seasonal.
components.coverageChange: Newly assessed coverage; not evidence that the event began on retrieval day.

components.title: National industrial electricity benchmark rises 4.7% year over year
components.summary: EIA’s 24 September release reports a July 2026 U.S. industrial average revenue of 9.77 cents/kWh, 4.7% above July 2025. This national proxy replaces an expired June state snapshot for coverage; it is not a Watershed tariff, bill or state-level comparison.
components.factorRationale: Exposure 80: Watershed advertises energy-dependent processing platforms, but kWh and tariffs are unknown. Severity 50: the national industrial benchmark is 4.7% higher year over year. Confidence 60: primary EIA data, discounted because a national average does not establish Illinois, Wisconsin or facility billing. Persistence 70: monthly cost-planning relevance without proof of contract reset. Velocity 35: lagged July data. Dependency 90: process energy is necessary. Substitutability 40: near-term process-energy alternatives may be limited, while tariff and efficiency options are unverified.
components.causalPath: National industrial electricity benchmark ↑ → possible applicable tariff or supply-contract reset → conditional processing and handling cost for freeze-dried, baked, roasted and popped platforms.
components.verify: Facility tariffs, demand charges, supply contracts, interval usage, effective cents/kWh, kWh per product and reset dates; no utility provider is assumed.
components.action: Finance and operations should compare actual effective cents/kWh and process energy use with plan; use the national series only as a screening benchmark.
components.trigger: Actual effective energy cost exceeds plan by >10% for two billing periods or an applicable utility/grid notice creates a verified continuity concern.
components.dateNote: EIA released July 2026 data on 24 September; national industrial average revenue per kWh is a price proxy. This revision is not directly comparable with the prior Illinois/Wisconsin June values.
components.coverageChange: A new national July benchmark restores energy coverage after the state snapshot expired. The measurement basis changed, so the lower model score is not evidence that Watershed energy exposure improved.

components.title: Packaging signals split between paperboard and plastics
components.summary: August PPI: paperboard +2.3% month over month (NSA) and +5.1% year over year; plastic resins -0.8% (SA); unsupported plastic film, sheet, and other shapes -0.5% (NSA), still +12.5% year over year. These categories are broader than food packaging.
components.factorRationale: Exposure 65: plausible film/carton dependence with specifications unknown. Severity 55: paperboard increase amid plastic monthly relief. Confidence 60: public indices but uncertain conversion into quotes. Persistence 65 and velocity 45: monthly changes and potential contract lag. Dependency 65: packaging requirement; substitutability 60: specification and customer approvals. Provisional analyst judgments.
components.causalPath: Paperboard/resin/converting cost changes → packaging vendor quotes and resets → conditional unit packaging cost and margins.
components.verify: Film structure, basis weight, print/conversion charges, carton specifications, resin/paperboard index clauses and contracted price lags.
components.action: Separate carton and film quote reviews; request evidence for index-linked adjustments rather than applying a blended packaging inflation rate.
components.trigger: Delivered packaging quotes exceed plan by >5% or a qualified vendor reports a material lead-time increase.
components.dateNote: Reference August 2026, preliminary. Annual and monthly changes are separate; the film series includes non-food shapes. Paperboard API is the same economic series, not independent corroboration.
components.coverageChange: Newly assessed coverage; not evidence that the event began on retrieval day.

components.title: Global CPG proxy shows mixed pet and snack demand with inventory pressure
components.summary: General Mills’ 23 September quarter reported North America Pet sales flat: pet treats grew low single digits, cat food double digits, dog food fell high single digits, and retailer inventory was a modest headwind. North America Retail organic sales fell 3% and U.S. Snacks declined mid-single digits. The company retained a cautious annual outlook while emphasizing protein, fiber and pet humanization. This is one archetype, not a Watershed customer or order signal.
components.factorRationale: Exposure 50: a relevant global CPG/pet archetype with no established Watershed account relationship. Severity 45: mixed category results and inventory pressure, not a confirmed order change. Confidence 70: primary quarterly disclosure, discounted for single-company and portfolio mismatch. Persistence 70: full-year outlook and inventory commentary. Velocity 35: quarterly evidence. Dependency 50: actual customer mix is unknown. Substitutability 70: multiple customer segments and platforms may diversify demand. Factors remain intentionally low for company impact.
components.causalPath: Archetype brand volumes, retailer inventories and innovation priorities → possible launch briefs, outsourcing appetite and order cadence → conditional Watershed sales pipeline.
components.verify: Actual customer segmentation; qualified briefs by pet treats, dog food, snacks, protein/fiber and other formats; retailer-inventory effects; pipeline stage; capacity and margin fit.
components.action: Sales and R&D should compare current qualified briefs with the mixed archetype signals, emphasizing validated pet-treat and protein/fiber problems while testing for snack or dog-food inventory drag before allocating capacity.
components.trigger: A verified customer changes orders, two additional primary archetypes corroborate the same volume/inventory move, or a qualified launch brief matches available capacity and validated controls.
components.dateNote: General Mills reported results on 23 September for the quarter ended 30 August 2026. Reported sales, organic sales and segment commentary are company-specific; no current Watershed customer relationship is inferred.
components.coverageChange: The scheduled quarterly recheck produced mixed demand evidence and specific innovation themes. Guidance changes from a generic cautious watch to category-by-category pipeline verification.

components.title: EIA’s export-constraint scenario supports a fuel watch
components.summary: EIA’s September outlook assumes Middle East export constraints through year-end and forecasts tight distillate inventories. This provides a conditional explanation for fuel exposure already tracked in S01, not a second independent loss estimate.
components.factorRationale: Exposure 65: global petroleum can affect domestic trucking without direct imports. Severity 70: distillate constraint scenario. Confidence 60: agency forecast, uncertain evolution. Persistence 80: year-end scenario; velocity 65: recent fuel moves. Dependency 75: conditional freight channel; substitutability 50: route/carrier choices do not fully replace diesel. Same fuel-cost issue group as S01; never added to it.
components.causalPath: Export/chokepoint constraints → global petroleum and distillate balance → domestic diesel benchmark → applicable carrier surcharge → delivered cost.
components.verify: Carrier surcharge formulas and lag, contractual pass-through, current EIA inventory releases and the assumptions behind the agency forecast; no Watershed import lane is asserted.
components.action: Use the same logistics/finance review as S01; run a conditional fuel-surcharge sensitivity instead of issuing a separate geopolitical alarm.
components.trigger: The observed relevant diesel benchmark or a contracted surcharge breaches the S01 trigger, or verified lane exposure changes.
components.dateNote: EIA forecast completed September 3 and released September 9. Projected inventories and export constraints are attributed scenarios, not realized measurements. No own forecast probability is created.
components.coverageChange: Newly assessed coverage; not evidence that the event began on retrieval day.

observations.title: Midwest diesel crosses the prior escalation trigger
observations.status: Reviewed; S01 severity and persistence increased; guidance changed
observations.finding: EIA reports Midwest on-highway diesel at $6.680/gal for 21 September, up $0.430 or 6.9% from 14 September. This follows the prior week’s 5.1% rise and crosses S01’s public-data trigger.
observations.causalPath: Regional retail diesel benchmark ↑ → applicable carrier fuel surcharge or freight quote ↑ → delivered input/outbound cost and conditional margin or service pressure.
observations.sourceScope: Regional retail benchmark only. No Watershed carrier, contract, surcharge, lane, invoice, customer pass-through or service impact is public.
observations.decision: Increase S01 severity 70→80 and persistence 70→80; retain exposure 75, confidence 70, velocity 80, dependency 80 and substitutability 35. Change guidance to immediate contract/invoice verification; do not activate the urgent safety/continuity override.

observations.title: New EIA release restores energy benchmark coverage on a national basis
observations.status: Reviewed; S10 refreshed with non-comparable national benchmark
observations.finding: EIA reports July 2026 U.S. industrial average revenue of 9.77 cents/kWh, up 4.7% from July 2025. The prior June Illinois/Wisconsin snapshot expired.
observations.causalPath: National industrial electricity benchmark ↑ → possible applicable tariff or supply-contract reset → conditional processing and handling cost for freeze-dried, baked, roasted and popped platforms.
observations.sourceScope: National price proxy, not a state or facility tariff. The revised score must not be interpreted as improvement from the prior state-level series.
observations.decision: Refresh S10 at 13.2/100 with factors 80/50/60/70/35/90/40 and a 25 October expiry; require actual bill and tariff validation.

observations.title: Global CPG archetype reports mixed pet and snack demand
observations.status: Reviewed; S12 refreshed; H2 evidence for and against expanded without confidence change
observations.finding: General Mills reported flat North America Pet sales, low-single-digit pet-treat growth, double-digit cat-food growth, high-single-digit dog-food decline, and a modest retailer-inventory headwind. North America Retail organic sales declined 3%, U.S. Snacks declined mid-single digits, and the annual outlook remains cautious while protein, fiber and pet humanization remain innovation priorities.
observations.causalPath: Archetype brand volumes, retailer inventories and innovation priorities → possible launch briefs, outsourcing appetite and order cadence → conditional Watershed sales pipeline.
observations.sourceScope: Single public-company archetype. No Watershed customer, order, mix, capacity allocation or production relationship is established.
observations.decision: Refresh S12 at 2.8/100; change sales guidance to category-specific pipeline verification. Add balanced H2 evidence and retain H2 confidence at 45, fail count 0 and OPEN outcome.

observations.title: FDA adds food recall notices without a Watershed match
observations.status: Unscored lead; no applicable exposure found
observations.finding: The FDA index lists apple sauce for patulin, alfalfa sprouting seeds for STEC/Salmonella, ground cinnamon for lead, pasta for undeclared shellfish and Greek peppers for possible pest contamination.
observations.causalPath: Only a verified ingredient, supplier, customer, SKU or lot match could create a Watershed quality or continuity pathway.
observations.sourceScope: Rolling, incomplete index. Listed products and firms are not attributed to Watershed, and row dates are not treated as event-onset dates.
observations.decision: Keep unscored. Quality should use normal match procedures only if a specific ingredient, supplier, customer, SKU or lot link emerges.

reviewNotes.challenge: Do the diesel, electricity and CPG releases establish Watershed outcomes?
reviewNotes.revision: No. Each primary observation is separated from inferred company exposure; no supplier, customer, contract, tariff, order, invoice or realized loss is claimed.

reviewNotes.challenge: Were factor changes selected to force a High posture?
reviewNotes.revision: No. S01 severity and persistence rise because the prior >5% weekly trigger was crossed twice consecutively; all other S01 factors stay fixed. S10 changes measurement basis and is explicitly non-comparable. S12 remains low-impact despite higher source confidence.

reviewNotes.challenge: Does nominal road-freight reliance prove surcharge pass-through or service risk?
reviewNotes.revision: No. The stronger action is to reconcile actual surcharge tables, lane mix, invoices and pass-through before operational commitments; the public benchmark alone does not prove cost or service impact.

reviewNotes.challenge: Does national electricity inflation quantify process or line cost?
reviewNotes.revision: No. S10 requires tariffs, demand charges, interval use and kWh per product; no production line, equipment load or state utility is inferred.

reviewNotes.challenge: Do the new FDA entries create a recall or contaminant event for Watershed?
reviewNotes.revision: No. The entries stay unscored until a verified ingredient, supplier, customer, SKU or lot match exists. Normal food-safety escalation remains separate from the executive score.

reviewNotes.challenge: Did new CISA candidates establish installed OT exposure?
reviewNotes.revision: No public asset inventory or product match exists. Cyber / OT remains null rather than zero, and no executive cyber persona is selected.

reviewNotes.challenge: Does the High posture require an urgent override or plant action?
reviewNotes.revision: No. The posture is a cost-risk priority driven by an external benchmark. The urgent override remains null because no safety event, outage, closure, route failure or facility disruption is established.

rechecks.note: Raised S01 severity and persistence after a second consecutive >5% Midwest diesel increase; refreshed national electricity and global CPG archetype components; kept facility/weather and Cyber/OT null and urgent override inactive.

latestRecheck.note: Raised S01 severity and persistence after a second consecutive >5% Midwest diesel increase; refreshed national electricity and global CPG archetype components; kept facility/weather and Cyber/OT null and urgent override inactive.

limits: Recorded 17–26 September snapshots provide only ten calendar points, insufficient for 30/90/365-day trend inference. Several intervening components expired before replacement; null is unassessed, not zero. Company exposure remains provisional and Cyber / OT remains unassessed.
